description: The zero-length literal (ISO §2023:8.3.3.1: 'If the opening and closing delimiters are contiguous, the length of the literal is zero, and it is known as a zero-length literal') in every spelling the alphanumeric, national and boolean formats admit - "", '', X"", N"", NX"", B"", BX"" (CobolLiteral.IsZeroLength). Not the same construct as ref-mod-zero-length-2023 (a reference modification of length zero). THE EDGE IS DERIVED, NOT QUOTED (VCR row 7.30; the repo holds no 1985/2002/2014 text, ratified decision #1): GnuCOBOL 3.2's per-standard dialect files carry zero-length-literals: unconformable in cobol85.conf AND cobol2002.conf and ok in cobol2014.conf - the method owner decision kb/Work R61 used for the debugging-mode window - and cobc -std=cobol2002 refuses MOVE "" TO X with 'zero-length literal does not conform to COBOL 2002'; Annex E (2014->2023) does not list it, so it predates 2023. Gated position-blind on the TOKEN by LiteralScreen.GateFormat (kb/Work PB895).
citation: ISO §2023:8.3.3.1; a COBOL-2014 introduction (derived: VCR row 7.30)
